inspection_summary: Inspected all 3475 splitlines-defined lines of the normalized article. The source develops Li-coefficient positivity through a decomposition into an explicitly estimable zeta sum and an arithmetic eta-coefficient sum, records exact bridges among eta, sigma, Stieltjes constants, and zeros, distinguishes proved bounds from conjectural cancellation, and extends the same architecture to Dirichlet, elliptic-curve, and Dedekind settings. Appendices supply alternative proofs, integral and hypergeometric comparison methods, trivial-zero subtraction, derivative and Mellin tools, zero-tail plausibility arguments, and Euler-Maclaurin refinement. Formula layout is sometimes fragile in the text layer, but the selected mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose and adjacent displayed equations; numerical tables and references were not promoted to semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Li positivity converts RH into a coefficient-sign problem
accepted_units.why_material: The text identifies analyticity after the map s=1/(1-z) and nonnegativity of every real Li coefficient as the necessary-and-sufficient RH interface used throughout the paper.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the conceptual reduction; the concrete coefficient definitions follow in the next accepted unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear; the exact xi normalization appears in an inline formula whose text extraction is usable.

accepted_units.title: Li coefficients as derivatives and sums over zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The same sequence is presented through logarithmic derivatives at one and zero and through reciprocal-power expressions over nontrivial zeros, connecting local analytic data to global zero geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the normalization caveat and the first logarithmic-derivative product relation needed to interpret the zero sum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed equations are layout-sensitive; checked prose fixes their roles, while exact symbol placement should be verified against source TeX before literal reuse.

accepted_units.title: Eta decomposition of each Li coefficient
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 decomposes lambda_n into an eta-binomial sum, an explicit alternating zeta-binomial sum, and elementary terms, while deriving eta from the Laurent expansion of zeta'/zeta and from von Mangoldt limits.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the central representation and includes enough differentiation and coefficient-extraction setup to avoid reconstructing the derivation externally.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core equations (10)-(15) are formula-dependent but readable in sequence; verify source TeX for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Equivalent discrete forms of the explicit S1 sum
accepted_units.why_material: Reordering the zeta Dirichlet series turns the finite binomial sum into sums of elementary kernels, creating monotone functions suitable for integral comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: The two forms support different estimates and motivate the later Appendix A comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (16)-(19); prose confirms the reordering mechanism despite multi-line formula layout.

accepted_units.title: Integral comparison gives an n log n lower bound for S1
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 compares a decreasing summand with an integral, changes variables, integrates by parts, evaluates with the digamma function, and transfers the result into lower and upper bounds for lambda_n modulo S2.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the theorem statement, complete monotonicity argument, and corollary so the direction and use of the inequality remain visible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact constants and integral kernels depend on displayed equations (20)-(24); checked prose makes the proof architecture recoverable.

accepted_units.title: The explicit-sum estimates port to generalized Li formulas
accepted_units.why_material: The paper maps parity-dependent Dirichlet and elliptic gamma-factor sums to S0, S1, and S3, explaining which already-estimated components can be reused for generalized hypotheses.
accepted_units.context_note: Detailed generalized formulas and arithmetic residuals are developed later in Appendices E and EII.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires equations (25)-(26) for exact mappings; prose clearly identifies the transfer.

accepted_units.title: Stieltjes-to-eta recursion from logarithmic differentiation
accepted_units.why_material: Equating (zeta'/zeta)zeta with zeta' yields a recursive bridge between familiar Stieltjes constants and the eta coefficients targeted by the Li decomposition.
accepted_units.context_note: The recurrence later supports finite computation and attempted inductive bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (27) is compact but layout-sensitive; its derivational identity is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Eta coefficients equal zero-power sums plus an explicit tail
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 3 connects sigma_k, the reciprocal-power sum over nontrivial zeros, to eta_{k-1} and an explicit zeta term; reordering and a generating identity evaluate the intervening zeta sum.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition of sigma, its relation to lambda, the full summation evaluation, and the alternative-proof pointer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies heavily on equations (28)-(39); semantic relations are recoverable, but exact binomial indices merit TeX verification.

accepted_units.title: Analytic evaluations constrain eta signs and moments
accepted_units.why_material: Evaluating and differentiating the Laurent series at several points produces sums, alternating sums, weighted moments, logarithmic sums, and a beta-weighted integral, ruling out a one-sign eta sequence and constraining decay.
accepted_units.context_note: These are exact aggregate constraints, not a proof of the later pointwise conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed series (40)-(44) are formula-sensitive; qualitative sign and moment conclusions are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Trivial-zero scale versus nontrivial-zero scale predicts eta alternation
accepted_units.why_material: Conjecture 1 separates four claims about sigma decay and eta alternation/size; the argument compares the first nontrivial-zero contribution with the explicit odd-integer tail and proves the stated triangle-inequality bound while leaving global magnitude control conjectural.
accepted_units.context_note: The span preserves both the numerical/heuristic status and the completed equations (47)-(48) needed after the original v1 cutoff.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The four-case expansion for sigma is extraction-fragile, but the competing decay scales and inequality logic are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Stieltjes bounds induce a recursive eta majorant
accepted_units.why_material: Known bounds for Stieltjes constants are inserted into the eta recursion to produce a possible inductive control, illustrating both a route and its weakness relative to Theorem 5.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an auxiliary bounding strategy, explicitly not the main conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact factorial coefficients in equations (49)-(51) require formula-layout care.

accepted_units.title: S2 cancellation is the unresolved bridge from eta behavior to Li positivity
accepted_units.why_material: The source conjectures square-root-scale growth for the eta-binomial sum S2 and combines it with the proved S1 bound to obtain an eventual positive lower bound for lambda_n, leaving only finitely many direct checks.
accepted_units.context_note: The implication is conditional on Conjecture 2; the source does not prove the needed magnitude correlation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (52)-(54) carry exact constants; prose makes the conditional dependency unambiguous.

accepted_units.title: Program summary isolates exponential cancellation and magnitude correlation
accepted_units.why_material: The discussion cleanly separates explicit sign alternation in S1, established or asserted eta sign alternation in S2, and the still-needed control relating consecutive eta magnitudes; it also states the proposed transfer to generalized L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: Useful as a limitation-aware map of proved, computed, and conjectural ingredients rather than as a new theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Predominantly prose; embedded formulas only name already-defined components.

accepted_units.title: The same comparison method bounds S0

accepted_units.context_note: This estimate later enters the parity split for generalized Li coefficients.

accepted_units.title: S3 comparison exposes parity-sensitive digamma structure
accepted_units.why_material: A weighted zeta sum is converted to an integral whose evaluation changes form with parity, furnishing the S3 term required by the elliptic-curve Li formula.

accepted_units.title: Binet's formula yields a two-sided digamma remainder bound
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiating Binet's representation isolates a positive-kernel remainder and produces a reusable two-sided correction to log z.
accepted_units.context_note: This supports error control in the preceding integral estimates.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (A.23)-(A.25) are sufficiently readable; exact endpoint assumptions should be retained from the source.

accepted_units.why_material: The source presents a Rice-type contour representation and explains asymptotic evaluation by contour displacement and residues, contrasting it with the paper's demand for non-asymptotic information.

accepted_units.why_material: Substituting the Mellin integral for zeta, changing variables, and subtracting the unit contribution independently evaluates the summation that links eta and sigma.

accepted_units.context_note: The source also flags a corrected typographical error in the antecedent reference.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet Li coefficients split into gamma growth and an arithmetic character sum
accepted_units.why_material: For primitive characters, the generalized Li coefficient is decomposed into an arithmetic von-Mangoldt/Laguerre sum and parity-dependent explicit terms, then bounded using S0 and S1; cancellation in character phases is explicitly conjectural.

accepted_units.title: Elliptic Li coefficients expose a signed prime-power residual

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed equations (E.15)-(E.18) are required for exact constants; the transform chain is readable.

accepted_units.why_material: Starting from the xi product, repeated logarithmic differentiation separates conductor, gamma-factor, and prime-power contributions and recovers the explicit Dirichlet Li formula.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (E.19)-(E.23) are symbol-dense; exact indices and conjugations should be checked against TeX.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact powers and shifts in equations (E.24)-(E.28) are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.why_material: The Dedekind completion is decomposed into discriminant, archimedean, and prime-ideal terms; differentiating supplies the candidate Li representation while explicitly leaving convergence justification as a gate.

accepted_units.title: A hypergeometric family unifies alternating zeta-sum bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Introducing a shift and multiplier turns several special sums into terminating 2F1 forms, whose comparison integrals become 3F2 expressions and reduce to digamma/harmonic forms at special parameters.
accepted_units.context_note: The inequality family subsumes S0, S1, and S3 comparison cases but does not automatically provide sharp bounds for every parameter.

accepted_units.title: Subtracting trivial-zero poles enlarges the eta expansion radius
accepted_units.why_material: Explicitly removing six trivial-zero contributions moves the nearest remaining singularity outward, yields faster-decaying modified eta coefficients, and changes the Li representation by known exponential terms.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a representation trade: improved coefficient scale is purchased with explicit zero corrections and constants lacking the earlier arithmetic interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (G.1)-(G.8) are extraction-sensitive; the radius change from 3 to 13 and its cause are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Trivial-zero derivatives calibrate the modified eta sequence
accepted_units.why_material: Taylor expansion at each trivial zero and functional-equation derivative identities provide modified coefficient data, including eta_0, and refine the lower-bound decomposition.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivative formulas support the preceding subtraction scheme rather than proving the remaining modified S2 bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The text layer around equations (G.9)-(G.15) is formula-fragile and should not be copied literally without TeX verification.

accepted_units.title: Functional-equation formulas relate zeta derivatives across the critical reflection
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiating the zeta functional equation relates negative-integer derivatives to positive-side values and Bernoulli series, supplying explicit data for modified eta moments.
accepted_units.context_note: The appendix presents examples and a general series rather than a complete closed calculus for all orders.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (H.1)-(H.6) have severe multi-line layout dependence; only the stated relation types are safe without TeX checking.

accepted_units.title: Mellin integrals generate logarithmic-derivative moments
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiating the Mellin representation of zeta produces formulas for zeta derivatives and successive derivatives of zeta'/zeta, directly targeting the weighted eta moments from the main text.
accepted_units.context_note: The method is open-ended and the source says it can be developed further.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (H.7)-(H.13) are layout-heavy; the differentiation pattern and intended application are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Li's polynomial as a Laguerre derivative and Mellin-Laplace kernel
accepted_units.why_material: The finite binomial polynomial is identified with a terminating confluent hypergeometric series and an associated Laguerre polynomial, converting its Mellin transform into a Laplace transform with a simple closed form.
accepted_units.context_note: This offers an orthogonal-polynomial viewpoint on the kernels already appearing in generalized Li sums.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (I.6)-(I.12) are sufficiently connected by prose, though exact signs should be checked against TeX.

accepted_units.title: Zero counting bounds an RH-conditional tail of sigma
accepted_units.why_material: A unit-interval zero-count estimate is combined with integral comparison to bound a reciprocal-ordinate tail, giving a concrete route from zero density to sigma decay.
accepted_units.context_note: The tail argument explicitly assumes RH and applies only beyond a very large threshold, so it cannot independently establish the conjectures it is meant to motivate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The equations are readable enough for the bounding chain, but exact constants and floors depend on displayed formulas (J.1)-(J.11).

accepted_units.title: A Dedekind xi integral forces real-axis derivative positivity
accepted_units.why_material: For an imaginary quadratic field, a positive integral kernel and the functional symmetry imply positivity of xi on the real axis, nonnegativity of derivatives on the right half-axis, and strict positivity for even orders.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a real-axis statement and does not locate complex zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (K.1) is visually complex, but the kernel positivity argument and derivative consequences are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Special-function series evaluate Dedekind xi derivative inputs
accepted_units.why_material: Theta-integral pieces are rewritten using incomplete gamma, error, and exponential-integral functions, and special derivative values are identified as inputs to Dedekind Li logarithmic derivatives.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an evaluation toolkit supporting the Dedekind extension, not a zero-location result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (K.4)-(K.10) are formula-dependent and partly fragmented; the special-function conversion is recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Euler-Maclaurin expansion refines S1 with a divergent correction series
accepted_units.why_material: Explicit summand derivatives are inserted into Euler-Maclaurin to refine the n log n contribution and suggest alternating upper/lower approximations while warning that the correction series is generally divergent.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposed bounds are described as expected approximations, not proved global inequalities.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (L.1)-(L.7) are layout-sensitive; the asymptotic status and sign-alternation mechanism are stated clearly.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Li positivity splits into explicit growth and arithmetic cancellation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The eta representation makes S1 an analytically controlled n log n contribution while concentrating the unresolved RH burden in cancellation and magnitude control for S2.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The S2 square-root bound is conjectural; sign alternation alone is insufficient, and the paper explicitly lacks consecutive-magnitude control.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zero-power sums mediate local Laurent data and Li coefficients
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Sigma provides a bridge from global zeros to eta Laurent coefficients and then through binomial transformation to lambda, allowing zero-scale heuristics and exact moment identities to constrain the proposed route.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The dominant-first-zero argument is asymptotic/plausibility evidence and does not prove the uniform eta bound needed by the Li criterion.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Trivial-zero subtraction trades explicit corrections for a larger analytic radius
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Removing known trivial-zero poles from zeta'/zeta shifts the convergence barrier from the first trivial zero to near the first nontrivial zero, producing faster-decaying modified coefficients plus explicit correction terms in lambda.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The modified coefficients lose the stated von-Mangoldt interpretation and their binomial sum still requires an independent bound.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Integral comparison is the portable deterministic component
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Reordering alternating zeta sums into monotone kernels enables integral, hypergeometric, and digamma comparisons that cover S0, S1, S3, and a parameterized family.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Portability of the explicit component does not control the separate prime-weighted arithmetic residuals.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Generalized Li formulas preserve the same arithmetic bottleneck
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Across Dirichlet, elliptic, and Dedekind completions, logarithmic differentiation separates conductor and gamma terms from prime or prime-ideal sums, so the architecture transfers while the cancellation problem changes weights.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Character phases or local sign changes are only plausibility for cancellation, and the Dedekind formula still carries an explicit convergence-justification gate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Alternative derivations test representation robustness
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The eta-sigma identity is recovered by discrete reordering, Mellin integration, and coefficient comparison, showing that the relation is not tied to one manipulation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Agreement among derivations validates the identity's internal representation, not the later conjectural decay assumptions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Euler-Maclaurin refines the solved term without removing the central obstruction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Asymptotic corrections can tighten S1's linear term and suggest alternating approximations, but further refinement of S1 leaves S2 magnitude control as the decisive missing ingredient.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The Euler-Maclaurin correction series is explicitly divergent and the proposed upper/lower approximations are not stated as proved uniform bounds.
